channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
item.description: It replaces hard-coded vocabulary-ID yes/no comparisons in POPE-style logit readouts with a tokenizer-derived token set covering the surface forms the model actually emits (e.g., ' Yes' vs 'Yes'). The cost is a one-time audit of generated tokens per model/tokenizer plus a slightly larger lookup set; no additional memory, latency, or compute in production. It can fail if adopted naively: tokenizer readouts must still be re-derived per model family, and cross-paper score comparisons remain invalid until readout and quantization precision are matched, since measured baseline shifts exceeded most published mitigation gains. 4 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks
item.description: FLICKER replaces centralized spectral decomposition of a horizontally partitioned matrix with federated power iteration that exchanges only matrix-vector products on local blocks, and BiFLICKER applies this to bipartite community detection. The cost is iterative cross-server communication rounds, a recursive grid search for spectral targets, and reliance on a reference server whose rescaled leading singular values must be valid global targets. It can fail when local sample sizes are too small for the reference server to estimate targets, when the data do not follow the assumed sparse bipartite stochastic block model, or when the horizontal partitioning assumption does not match the deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: MX-Like Tensor Core for LLM Inference with NPU Integration via Hardware-Software Co-Design Exploration
item.description: The work does not replace a software technique; it replaces ad hoc selection of block-scaled quantization formats (OCP MX, NVFP4) with a systematic HW-SW co-design exploration of scale, weight, and activation format combinations on a specialized NPU MAC datapath. For a software practitioner the actionable finding is narrow: scale format choice matters mainly under aggressive FP4 quantization, where UE5M3 scales improve accuracy at negligible silicon cost. Adoption fails at the reader's constraints because the gains are realized only in custom NPU silicon (SNAX platform), cannot be enabled on a commodity 24 GB GPU or third-party API, and the perplexity results may not transfer across models or calibration pipelines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Multilingual Voicemail and Answering Machine Detection via Pretrained Audio Embeddings and Gradient Boosting Machines
item.description: The method replaces proprietary answering machine detection systems and computationally expensive real-time models (including ASR-plus-LLM pipelines) with frozen pretrained audio embeddings feeding a gradient boosting classifier. Cost is low: no GPU or fine-tuning is required for inference, training reduces to fitting a GBM on extracted embeddings, and the authors release a 500+ recording, 7-language dataset (OpenAMD) for replication. What can fail: the dataset is small for a production telephony system, per-language and per-gender performance differences were found statistically significant, and robustness degrades under additive noise and packet loss typical of real carrier networks. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reliable Before Profitable: QuantHarness for Governing Financial Strategy Development with LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces ad-hoc single-agent or loosely scripted LLM pipelines for turning natural-language research requests into backtested financial strategies, substituting a structured workflow (specification, data grounding, construction, testing, review) with enforced stage-level information, action, and commitment boundaries. The cost is additional orchestration complexity, structured run-record storage, and extra LLM calls across stages, which raises latency and API spend per strategy developed. What can fail: the benchmark (FinRelBench) is introduced by the same authors, so the 90.72% figure may not transfer to real trading desks; boundary rules can block legitimate repairs or add friction without catching novel leakage modes; and the paper demonstrates violation containment only under its own controlled stress tests, not under production data or live-market conditions. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Provable Adversarial Detection: Prime Quantization meets Gromov--Wasserstein
item.description: The method replaces heuristic adversarial detectors (e.g., feature-density or statistics-based screens) with a detector that compares sample geometry across a CNN embedding space and a prime-quantized space, using Gromov–Wasserstein discrepancy with claimed separation guarantees. It adds per-inference cost: an extra embedding pass, a quantization mapping, and a GW-style distance computation, plus implementation complexity, without quantified latency or memory figures in the abstract. It can fail against adaptive attacks crafted to preserve geometry in both spaces, and its guarantees likely depend on the specific threat model, attack strength bounds, and embedding choices validated in the paper's experiments. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Hybrid GPU and Processing-Near-Memory Architecture with Shared DRAM for Efficient Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
item.description: DuoPD replaces GPU-side prefill-decode disaggregation and SM partitioning by executing full decoding on Processing-Near-Memory units in the HBM logic die while prefill runs on the GPU, sharing the HBM interface via TSV-level bandwidth allocation. The cost is entirely hardware-side: it requires custom PNM silicon, a new microarchitecture, and a hierarchical data-mapping scheme, with no software-only path to deployment. It can fail commercially if no memory vendor ships such parts, and technically if bandwidth sharing between GPU and PNM does not hold under real serving skew between prefill and decode load. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Holistic Buoyancy-Driven Cloud Native Resource Management
item.description: The method replaces static resource requests and prior workload profiling in Kubernetes scheduling with runtime 'buoyancy' signals that measure each workload's sensitivity to shared resources such as last-level cache and memory bandwidth, driving adaptive scheduling, node-local allocation, and limited rescheduling. It costs a Kubernetes-native control plane extension, continuous runtime instrumentation of workloads, and a multi-node cluster to provide rescheduling headroom, plus ongoing maintenance of the sensitivity-measurement framework. It can fail when buoyancy estimates are inaccurate or unstable under rapidly shifting workload mixes, when rescheduling triggers migration overhead or disruption, and its benefits are unproven outside the evaluated congestion regimes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
item.description: It replaces chunk-bounded speculative execution, where generation is truncated or restarted at each speech update, with periodic Thinker invocations that let ongoing reasoning and dispatched tool calls run to completion against the latest partial transcript and a shared results record. The cost is additional inference calls during listening (raising token/API spend), plus orchestration complexity for managing concurrent invocations and a shared state record. It can fail when partial transcripts mislead speculative tool calls into wasted or incorrect executions, and the paper notes final task quality effects are benchmark-dependent, so gains may not transfer to a given workload. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AudioScorer: Learning Question-Aware Token Relevance for Large Audio Language Models
item.description: It replaces heuristic audio-token pruning (attention, similarity, temporal sampling) with a lightweight learned scorer that ranks tokens by relevance to the user question, distilled from the frozen LALM's answer-gradient saliency plus answer supervision. The cost is a one-time training/distillation stage that needs gradient access to a self-hosted frozen LALM, an added per-question scoring step in inference, and retained quality that depends on the chosen retention rate. It can fail on out-of-distribution questions or acoustic content where the scorer mis-ranks tokens, is unavailable for API-only models without gradients, and may degrade tasks that depend on dense temporal detail at aggressive retention. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions
item.description: The method replaces informal judgment of agent trustworthiness with reproducible trade-log tests that measure rule adherence (stops, targets, position limits, regime-conditional risk) before capital is committed. Cost is modest: the published trade snapshot, Bitcoin prices, and regime labels suffice to rerun the tests, but the methodology assumes agents that declare strategies and risk parameters upfront, and building equivalent instrumentation for a new agent is real engineering work. It can fail by producing false confidence: rule-following is shown to be orthogonal to profitability, sample sizes are small (2,627 positions, one unprofitable agent), and results are trade-level, not account-level returns. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Generic On-Board AI Processing Chain for Earth Observation: From Application Development to Embedded Deployment and Mission-Level Orchestration
item.description: The method replaces ground-station processing of full downlinked scenes with an on-board chain of int8-quantized inference on FPGA, a reusable tiler-inference-mosaicer workflow, and unikernel-packaged steps orchestrated by a cloud-native on-board orchestrator. The cost is substantial embedded-engineering effort: model quantization and hardware porting, plus adoption of specialized unikernel packaging and orchestration infrastructure, none of which runs on a conventional GPU workstation. Adoption can fail through quantization-induced accuracy loss on new tasks, hardware-specific toolchain friction, and orchestration overhead on constrained space-grade compute. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
item.description: VibeTraining-Bench replaces ad hoc manual tuning of data, trainer, and inference harness with a standardized benchmark that measures whether research agents can perform that co-design iteratively under a fixed budget. It costs substantial compute per run, since each episode requires repeated training and evaluation cycles inside isolated containers with anti-reward-hacking safeguards. It can fail to transfer: strong results by frontier research agents on this benchmark do not imply a small team with one 24 GB GPU can replicate the iterative training loops, and residual reward-hacking or overfitting to validation feedback remains possible. 2 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Autonomous intelligence for mining productivity: a multi-agent AI approach to operational value creation
item.description: EI2ROC proposes a three-tier multi-agent architecture (LLM orchestrator plus specialised monitoring and production-capacity agents over an MCP-style tool interface) intended to replace manual, siloed supervision in mining Integrated Remote Operation Centres, alongside a six-dimension benchmarking framework for industrial agentic systems. It costs orchestration complexity, LLM inference cost and latency per decision in a safety-critical setting, and the paper itself marks most components as reference design or future work, with only preliminary cost and latency observations from one site. It can fail through orchestrator errors propagating to SCADA-connected actions, unmet real-time and regulatory-auditability requirements, and the absence of validated benchmarks for the industrial blind spot the paper identifies. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: An Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
item.description: The recipe replaces full fine-tuning of MoE models (and adapters that bypass experts) with LoRA/DoRA applied directly to native expert weights, trained without a load-balancing auxiliary loss since no nonzero coefficient Pareto-dominated the zero baseline. Cost is limited to a small trainable-parameter budget (17% fewer than the module-bypass baseline) within a single-GPU fine-tuning run, plus a measured 3.2-point average downstream regression for the redesigned variant. Failure modes include expert routing drift degrading general-knowledge retention, results transferring poorly across the three studied backbones to other MoE architectures, and task-specific sensitivity to which experts and ranks are adapted. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CTLite: Lightweight Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Reusable Continuous-Time Summaries
item.description: CTLite replaces learned temporal encoders for irregular multivariate time series with a parameter-free continuous-time moment encoder whose summaries are cached and reused across optimization steps and repeated queries, leaving only a small damped-extrapolation plus low-rank cross-variable readout to train. It costs almost nothing in parameters or latency and runs on a single small GPU or even CPU-class hardware, but it adds a preprocessing and caching layer and its accuracy claim is only best-or-second-best rather than uniformly superior. It can fail where the moment-based local level and trend summaries are a poor fit for the dynamics, on datasets unlike the four evaluated benchmarks, or when histories change frequently enough to negate the reuse benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories
item.description: PACE replaces ad hoc or issue-resolution-style evaluation of coding agents with evidence-based scoring of full PRD fulfillment against 750 expert-audited Code Points in mature repositories. It costs evaluation engineering effort: tasks must be adapted or the benchmark adopted as-is, expert-style auditing is labor-intensive, and running 43 enterprise tasks against candidate model-scaffold configurations consumes API budget. It can fail as a selection signal because even the best configuration achieves only a 14.0% complete-delivery rate, so benchmark ranking may not translate into dependable autonomous delivery on the reader's own repositories. 1 independent implementation, 1 star. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: R2-GP: Variance-Calibrated Priors for Additive Gaussian Processes
item.description: R2-GP replaces independent priors on component amplitudes in Matérn-kernel additive Gaussian process models with a single global R2 prior that allocates each component's variance contribution after rescaling by length-scale and observed inputs. It costs a reparameterisation of the prior and, for large datasets, adoption of Hilbert space kernel approximations, adding modelling complexity without reducing compute. It can fail if the chosen global R2 prior is misspecified, if the spectral approximation degrades kernel fidelity at small length-scales, or in regimes where the independent-prior baseline was already adequate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Fake News, Real Crashes: Information Injection Attacks on LLM Financial Trading Agents
item.description: The paper does not replace an existing method; it is an attack benchmark that supersedes informal red-teaming of news-consuming LLM agents, and it evaluates candidate defenses including hierarchical aggregation of evidence. Adopting its lessons costs added inference calls and latency (hierarchical aggregation and credibility-cue checking require extra model passes) plus engineering effort to validate and annotate untrusted feed items. Defenses can fail because attack success is state-dependent (91% ASR against an agent about to hold, 12% against one about to buy), generalizes across model vendors, and remains effective when fake items are blended unlabeled into real feeds, while surface credibility cues alone drive success regardless of claim content. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards
item.description: It replaces prompted foundation-model judges (4B to GPT-5.4 scale, plateaued at 68%-70% agreement) with a small trainable Judge, as small as 1B, that learns what to check and when to stop via online RL while a frozen Probe executes checks in the live environment. The cost is an online RL training loop requiring interactive OSWorld-style environments, single-attempt verification per terminal state, and return normalization across states, plus engineering to couple the Judge to a live GUI sandbox. It can fail when target environments differ from the training distribution despite the reported cross-benchmark transfer, when reward agreement gains do not translate to Actor task success on a specific workload, or when the team cannot maintain the live-environment training infrastructure. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: On Learning Expand-and-Sparsify Representations
item.description: The method replaces a dense ReLU layer (and its random-map expand-and-sparsify variant) with a learned linear expansion followed by top-k sparsification, letting the expansion be much narrower than the exponential widths random theory requires while matching the dense layer's accuracy at 10% activation density. The cost is an extra learned linear map and top-k selection per layer, plus the need to tune expansion width and sparsity per task; the evidence base is 73 OpenML classification and 48 regression tasks, all small tabular benchmarks, not production-scale deep networks. It can fail because the learned-map advantage vanishes at wide expansions, gains over dense ReLU are parity rather than improvement, and results on small tabular data may not transfer to the reader's actual workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AfriGuard: Safety and Robust Refusal For African Languages
item.description: AfriGuard replaces general-purpose or larger off-the-shelf guardrail models for safety classification and refusal detection in African languages with a culturally grounded evaluation dataset plus supervised fine-tuned smaller classifiers. Costs include fine-tuning on the released dataset, maintaining per-deployment classifiers in the inference path (added latency and a failure point), and dependence on dataset coverage of the 10 included languages and safety categories. It can fail on languages or dialects outside the dataset, on culturally specific harm expressions not represented in training data, and because the paper shows models often produce linguistically inadequate responses rather than proper refusals, a detector may report incidental non-assistance as safe behavior. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing
item.description: RouterWorld replaces ad hoc, accuracy-only router evaluation with a standardized benchmark that treats latency as a first-class metric and models realistic partial observability (cold-start logs and streaming data). Adopting it costs integration effort against its LLM-as-a-judge protocol and does not itself provide a production router; the reader still needs to select or train one of the baseline routing methods. It can fail to transfer if the reader's query distribution, candidate model set, or hardware latency profile diverges from the benchmark's assumptions, and its LLM-as-a-judge quality labels may not match the reader's task-specific quality bar. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting
item.description: ReAnchor replaces the fixed single-block diffusion draft by reanchoring a pretrained drafter at shifted positions using verifier hidden states that standard speculative decoding discards after the first rejection, generating parallel draft blocks that extend coverage beyond the original block endpoint. It is training-free, so the cost is limited to implementation complexity and modest extra compute for the additional reanchored draft blocks, with no retraining or extra model weights. Gains can shrink or vanish at sampling temperatures above zero, depend on a compatible block diffusion drafter such as DFlash, and may not transfer to workloads or target models outside the evaluated set. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed
item.description: The method replaces drop-oldest-turn context truncation in agent harnesses with summarization of prior turns plus an explicit invitation for the model to take notes. It costs additional tokens per turn for summary generation and added harness complexity, and provider-native reasoning replay may be needed to recover the remaining gap. It can fail when a required fact is never re-observable and the summary or notes omit it, and the ARC-AGI-3 numbers are single-run point estimates that may not transfer to other benchmarks or models. 2 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback
item.description: RELIEF replaces training pipelines that ignore post-generation interactive behavior by having a coding agent revise generated interfaces from feedback (code inspection, automated interaction, human comments, and interaction recordings) and folding those revisions back into the original generation traces as fine-tuning supervision. Its cost is a feedback-collection effort (the study used 200 websites, 355 interaction recordings, 24 users), agent revision runs, and fine-tuning compute, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU only for small models or via API-based fine-tuning. It can fail when feedback is noisy or sparse, when the base model is too weak to benefit (effectiveness depends on base capability), and when improvements in revised traces do not transfer to zero-shot generation of new interfaces. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
item.description: CC-Gittins replaces exhaustive or ad-hoc evaluation of model-to-role assignments in multi-model agentic workflows with a cost-aware multi-objective bandit search that reuses each evaluation for both quality-seeking and cost-seeking. It costs the implementation of a Gittins-index search loop plus uncertainty-adjusted quality and cost tracking per candidate, with a small inference overhead per batch but no additional model training. It can fail when the search budget is too small to clear the frontier, when uncertainty estimates are miscalibrated for the user's task distribution, or when the workflow has so few roles and candidate models that exhaustive evaluation is already cheap. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
item.description: The method replaces single-token autoregressive decoding with parallel generation of mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass, trained via a variational objective combining autoregressive and parallel decoding losses. It requires pretraining the model with this objective from scratch, so it cannot be applied to existing pretrained checkpoints, and the reported speedups depend on latent-variable routing that adds training and inference complexity. Failure modes include quality degradation on tasks where token dependencies are poorly captured by the latent variables, and the power-law speedup claim is validated only up to 3B parameters, leaving behavior at production model scales unverified. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics
item.description: HoloCosm replaces full-benchmark evaluation and single-metric sample-selection methods by selecting a small subset of samples that jointly minimizes score-reconstruction error across multiple metrics while constraining ranking distortion. It costs an offline optimization pass over existing model scores on the full benchmark, meaning it requires score data from a population of source models and adds selection complexity before it saves any compute. It can fail when applied to models outside the source population used for selection, when metric correlations shift, or when too few historical model scores exist to calibrate the compressed subset, in which case random sampling may match or beat it. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models
item.description: recAMPLIFY replaces parameter scaling in masked protein language models with a weight-tied recursive Transformer core that refines hidden states over a variable number of cycles, optionally with a Gated Mixture Recurrence decoder for adaptive depth. The recipe requires large-scale pretraining (2T tokens), which exceeds the reader's infrastructure and budget; only released checkpoints, if published, would make GMR's adaptive-depth inference usable, and GMR's accuracy trade-off is task-dependent and can be negative. Recursive weight-tying can become unstable beyond the trained depth (the paper's own gating analysis addresses this), and the method is specific to masked protein encoders, not general LLM workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
item.description: TokenGate replaces full-sequence prefill, in which every input token passes through all layers, with a learned gating component that scores and prunes tokens via token-gated attention added to an existing pretrained model. The cost is a lightweight adaptation step comparable to parameter-efficient fine-tuning, plus the integration and maintenance of a nonstandard attention mechanism in the serving stack. It can fail on workloads where pruned tokens carry task-critical information, where the pruning distribution shifts from the adaptation data, or where short-to-medium contexts make the TTFT gain too small to justify the added complexity. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
item.description: The method replaces fitting fixed readouts on frozen pretrained backbones (or costly full fine-tuning) with LoRA adapters plus a lightweight readout on large multimodal backbones, exploiting causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in one pass instead of sliding windows. Costs include access to large backbones (up to 104B parameters, requiring API access or multi-GPU inference beyond a single 24 GB card for the largest models), training complexity of joint multi-LoRA training, and the need for expensive fMRI/MEG-style neural recording data. It can fail if the reader lacks aligned neural-stimulus datasets, if the backbone's causal structure does not match the temporal sampling of the neural data, or if LoRA rank and readout capacity are insufficient for a given brain region or modality. 1 independent implementation, 2 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
item.description: This replaces rule-based or myopic (single-step uplift/response-model) next-best-action targeting with a Constrained MDP solved via linear programming, integrating causal off-policy correction of customer dynamics and yielding shadow prices for constraint trade-offs. The cost is not GPU compute but data and modeling effort: it requires logged customer-intervention data with adequate coverage, a defensible state representation (the paper uses RFM stages), causal estimation of transition dynamics, and LP machinery rather than standard supervised pipelines. Failure modes include misspecified causal dynamics that invalidate the off-policy correction, OPE that relies on a learned model rather than a randomized holdout (so the 19% figure may not transfer to live traffic), state aggregation that hides heterogeneity, and constraint shadow prices that mislead if the LP formulation omits real operational couplings. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
item.description: The method replaces full-context KV caching and external retrieval augmentation with memory internalized in model state via Gated DeltaNet-2 updates and a Mixture-of-Storage layer. It costs a full training pipeline (continued pre-training plus post-training on 34B tokens over a prepared backbone), a nonstandard architecture with custom training and inference infrastructure, and reported parity rather than superiority against retrieval-augmented methods. It can fail because the claimed gains are tied to the authors' released MemT checkpoints and infrastructure, long-horizon memory quality may degrade on workloads unlike their evaluations, and there is no drop-in path for existing API-based models. 4 independent implementations, 304 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
item.description: RefCraft replaces idealized webpage-generation evaluations (single-screenshot reconstruction or text-only instructions) with 300 multimodal tasks combining instructions and one to five reference screenshots, scored via keypoints plus programmatic and VLM judges. It costs nothing in model deployment but requires API or GPU budget to run candidate models through render-inspect-refine loops, and the VLM-judge component adds evaluation variance and API cost. It can fail as a selection signal if the reader's production tasks differ from webpage development, if VLM judge scores are noisy or gameable, or if benchmark overfitting substitutes for real user evaluation. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
item.description: WildAWM replaces reliance on human-collected computer-use trajectories and hand-built training environments with an open-source-model pipeline that synthesizes executable GUI/MCP/CLI environments, tasks, and execution-based verifiers. It costs a full environment-generation and agent-training workflow: heterogeneous rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, counterfactual probes, and fine-tuning runs, which is feasible with open models but exceeds casual experimentation on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail if synthetic tasks drift from real-world distributions, if verifiers reward incorrect trajectories that pass the quality gates, or if gains do not transfer to the reader's specific target applications. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
item.description: The method replaces a classical supervised classifier with a parameterized data-dependent Hamiltonian whose approximate ground state defines the decision rule, trained and executed on quantum processors. It costs access to quantum hardware (demonstrated on IBM Heron processors), a quantum ground-state approximation subroutine, and a hybrid training pipeline, none of which fit a 24 GB GPU or standard API budget. It can fail through noise and limited qubit counts on current hardware, unproven practical advantage over classical baselines on real workloads, and dependence on cryptographic assumptions for its classical-hardness claim. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
item.description: The study evaluates replacing in-context tool outputs with file-based retrieval (section indexes) in agent harnesses, and proposes mitigations: explicitly naming the authoritative output file or inlining outputs that fit. Retrieval saves context window space, but for GPT-5.x models it costs 8-11 accuracy points; the naming prompt costs essentially nothing and recovers most of the loss. The residual failure mode is evidence substitution: the agent computes correctly but answers from its own higher-precision intermediate files, misrounding to a neighboring option, and prompting for correct rounding does not fix this. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
item.description: WeAct replaces joint fine-tuning and static adapter merging by training independent capability-specific LoRA adapters on a frozen backbone and letting the agent select adapters at runtime through its native tool-calling interface. The cost is maintaining and serving multiple adapters (each small, but adding routing complexity), plus training a selection policy whose adapter-switching actions must be learned from trajectories. It can fail if the model selects the wrong adapter mid-trajectory, if switching breaks contextual coherence across stages, or if the benchmark gains do not transfer to workloads with fewer or less distinct capability boundaries. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
item.description: FunCAD-Harness replaces visual plausibility checks and generic simulation passes with candidate-specific physical tests that translate abstract functional requirements into executable verification of LLM-generated CAD mechanisms. Adoption costs a physics simulation stack (CAD modeling, kinematic/dynamic simulators), test-generation logic per candidate design, and iterative agent-simulation loops that increase latency and API token spend per design. It can fail where requirements are too underspecified to operationalize as tests, where simulators diverge from real manufacturing tolerances, and it transfers only partially to domains outside mechanical CAD. 2 independent implementations, 7 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BS-Spec: BFP-Based Bit-Sharing for Self-Speculative LLM Decoding with LUT-Driven Mixed-Precision Acceleration
item.description: BS-Spec replaces separate draft models and their KV caches by deriving drafts from a single block-floating-point target model, partially loading the most significant bits of weights and KV cache with shared exponents, plus offline calibration and a runtime precision lookup table. The reported gains depend on a custom mixed-precision BFP accelerator with an LUT-based variable-precision datapath, so realizing them costs specialized hardware, a calibration pipeline per serving regime, and BFP reformatting of model weights. On commodity GPUs the speedup may not materialize, acceptance rates can degrade under aggressive bit truncation for some workloads, and the per-regime calibration must be redone when the workload mix shifts. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ToPA: Block-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine-Tuning
item.description: ToPA replaces low-rank (LoRA-style) or sparse update matrices with products of block-wise Toeplitz matrices, which impose no explicit rank or sparsity constraint and can approximate arbitrary updates with short factor chains. The cost is a non-standard parameterization: it is not supported by mainstream PEFT libraries, so adoption requires integrating custom code, and per-layer parameter count and compute depend on block size and chain length, which must be tuned against a LoRA baseline. It can fail if gradient instability persists for deeper chains, if the expressivity gain does not transfer to the reader's specific task, or if the method remains a research-stage implementation without maintained tooling. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Conformal Policy Selection: When to Deploy AI Decisions for Targeted Intervention
item.description: It replaces ad hoc thresholding or average-effect criteria for deciding which individuals receive an AI-recommended treatment, substituting a multiple-testing procedure with weighted conformal p-values that bounds the false discovery rate among selected units. The cost is a held-out calibration set collected under the behavior policy, fitted propensity and outcome models, and added pipeline complexity rather than extra GPU or inference budget. It can fail under covariate shift beyond what the importance weights cover, when both nuisance models are misspecified simultaneously, or when calibration data are too scarce for the weighted conformal quantiles to be informative. 0 independent implementations, 1573 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Towards Hyperparameter Transfer for Differentially Private Optimization
item.description: DP-μP replaces per-width learning-rate sweeps (and standard μP, which the paper shows breaks under DP) with layer-wise learning-rate scaling rules derived from a signal-to-noise condition for gradient clipping and noise injection. The cost is implementing a modified parametrization and spectral scaling scheme in the training code, which adds complexity and constrains architectural choices, though inference cost is unchanged. The method can fail when assumptions behind the SNR condition are violated, such as atypical clipping thresholds, noise multipliers, or architectures far from those validated, and the results concern width transfer from scratch rather than fine-tuning of pretrained models. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference
item.description: Prism Attention replaces rigid cross-layer sharing of sparse attention indices (computed once at anchor layers and statically reused) with a coarse-to-fine proposal-and-refinement scheme that exploits the localized shift of salient tokens between layers. The cost is additional per-layer refinement logic and index management on top of a sparse-attention implementation, plus the integration complexity of a non-standard attention path rather than stock FlashAttention. It can fail on workloads whose attention patterns do not exhibit the assumed cross-layer locality, and realized speedup depends heavily on whether an efficient implementation of the proposal-refinement step exists for the reader's serving stack. 2 independent implementations, 127 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Distinguishability and Recovery for a Doubly Sparse Spiked Wigner Model
item.description: This is a theoretical random-matrix statistics paper on detecting and recovering a sparse rank-one signal in a spiked Wigner model; it does not replace any component of an LLM production stack. Its cost is irrelevant to the reader because the contribution consists of statistical thresholds, recovery guarantees, and a leave-one-out quadratic thresholding algorithm analyzed asymptotically, not an implementable inference or training optimization. Nothing fails after adoption because there is nothing to adopt for an engineer running one 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: PairSight: Characterizing and Predicting Operator-Level Interference in GPU Sharing for DNN Inference
item.description: PairSight replaces binary compute-memory rules, standalone scaling curves, and model-level predictors used to estimate interference when co-locating DNN inference tasks on one GPU, using hardware-counter-based operator-level modeling of shared-memory-path contention. The cost is a profiling and training pipeline: collecting hardware counters for operator pairs, training the predictor, and integrating its predictions into a scheduler, which adds engineering complexity beyond simple heuristics. It can fail if the reader's serving stack lacks counter access (e.g., third-party APIs), if co-location pairs differ from profiled hardware behavior, or if the reader only ever runs one model per GPU, in which case there is no interference to predict. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
item.description: Replaces autoregressive answer generation and prompt-based classification with a single forward pass that extracts candidate-letter logits at the final position and normalizes them over valid options, unifying Boolean, categorical, and ordinal decisions in one interface. Costs: a dedicated Chinese-language checkpoint (0.8B or 2B, Q8-quantizable) rather than a general-purpose LLM, giving one-token latency and small memory footprint, but requiring adoption of the authors' task-specific model and pipeline instead of existing API models. Can fail: results are Chinese-language and decision-formatted only, the 2B model does not yet beat the 0.8B on professional domains, temperature scaling shifts some individual predictions, and no isolation of scale effects or comparison against strong prompted general models is established. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Response-Informed Value Estimation for Cost-Aware Multi-Turn LLM Routing
item.description: RIVET replaces static or outcome-only-trained multi-turn model routing with turn-level routing trained via two value estimators, one of which conditions on the realized response during training only. It costs an offline training pipeline over logged trajectories, two value networks, and labeled task outcomes, plus per-turn scoring overhead at deployment; routing itself stays pre-call and cheap. It can fail when logged trajectories are scarce or off-distribution relative to production traffic, when candidate model prices or behaviors change after training, and on benchmarks unlike MINT where response-informed credit assignment may transfer poorly. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Towards Agentic Proof Harness Engineering
item.description: The method replaces manual proof-harness engineering, in which verification engineers write symbolic inputs, initialization code, and dependency models for a target unit, with an LLM coding agent that constructs and refines harnesses under formal soundness and precision guards. It costs an agentic LLM workflow plus a working formal-verification toolchain such as CBMC, and the evaluation covers only three pre-existing bugs in two C projects, so there is no measured speed, cost, or coverage improvement. It can fail through unsound or imprecise dependency abstractions that the guards miss, targets outside the demonstrated C/CBMC setting, and projects lacking suitable assertion-level properties. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
item.description: Replaces reporting only attack success rate (ASR) in indirect prompt-injection evaluation with a failure-mode decomposition (refused vs. ignored vs. task-not-completed) using the paper's Attack-Task Outcome Matrix and a label-blind LLM judge, whose prompt and code are released. Cost is one judge pass over agent trajectories plus the labeled corpus, feasible on a single GPU or via API, with no changes to the production agent required. It can fail if the LLM judge misclassifies refusal versus ignoring at scale, and the findings are specific to small open-weight agents (2-14B) on InjecAgent and AgentDojo, so results may not transfer to other models or benchmarks. 2 independent implementations, 15 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ADT: All-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures
item.description: ADT replaces atom-level token sequences and residue-only protein tokens with a compact discrete representation (one token per small-molecule atom, one per protein residue) whose quantization loss is repaired by a diffusion decoder instead of deterministic decoding. It costs the training and inference overhead of a diffusion model on top of the tokenizer and autoregressive generator, plus domain-specific data and evaluation pipelines. It can fail through residual geometric distortion from quantization that the diffusion step does not fully recover, and the abstract reports no validated downstream metrics (e.g., binding, synthesizability), so reconstruction quality may not translate to useful generated molecules. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents
item.description: JointCore replaces singleton-record deletion and relevance-ranked retrieval with relevance-cost-ordered group deletion that tests blocks of records before individuals when selecting a minimal sufficient memory subset for LLM agents. Its cost is additional subset evaluations and a more complex deletion procedure, and the authors explicitly state it is a benchmark baseline on JointCoreBench rather than deployment-ready memory compression. Behavior is interface-dependent: physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, and counterfactual values produce different results, so sufficiency guarantees established under the deterministic primary interface may not transfer to a production memory store. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Annotrace: A Workbench for Step-Level Annotation of Agent Traces
item.description: Annotrace replaces the per-study practice of hand-building throwaway scripts to label agent failure traces, importing six trace formats (OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith, Langfuse among them) into an ordered, nested step list with a user-defined codebook, AI-proposed starting labels, and inter-annotator agreement measurement between human and model annotators. It costs only local tooling plus frontier-model API calls for label proposal and pre-annotation, with no GPU, cluster, or training requirement, fitting the constrained infrastructure directly. It can fail if the model-proposed codebook biases the human codebook toward the model's own error categories, if AI pre-answers anchor human judgment and inflate measured agreement, and if the six supported formats do not cover the team's actual tracing stack. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: From Memory Hits to Answerable Evidence: Query-Conditioned Memory Compilation for Long-Term Agent Memory
item.description: MemCompile replaces the common pattern of passing retrieved or expanded memory units directly to the reader with a two-plane pipeline: an Address Plane that locates relevant support via compact descriptors and capacity-aware cells, and an Evidence Plane that allocates a bounded evidence budget across complementary packets and renders only retained claims into the final context. It costs additional pipeline complexity, extra query-conditioned processing stages (normalization, budgeting, rendering) that add latency and likely extra model calls per query, and requires implementing a non-trivial framework rather than a drop-in component. It can fail if the descriptors or cell capacities mislocate evidence, if the budget allocator drops necessary complementary packets, or if gains measured on LoCoMo and LongMemEval do not transfer to the reader's conversational distribution. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentOnto: Ontology-Guided LLM Agents for Enterprise Data Analytics
item.description: Replaces ad hoc prompt-only agents that connect analytical requests to databases and documents without an explicit knowledge representation, substituting a curated ontology that guides analysis and absorbs confirmed feedback. Costs include building and maintaining the ontology, an iterative preparation phase with self-generated tasks, and added orchestration complexity around the LLM, though inference itself runs on standard API access. Can fail if the ontology is incomplete or drifts from the underlying schemas, if confirmed feedback is sparse or wrong, or if enterprise data access and document quality do not match the evaluation setting. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SETAREH Transform: A Sorting-Assisted Haar-Wavelet Sparsification Method for Approximate Inner-Product Computation
item.description: The method replaces exact full-dimension inner products between a fixed weight vector and successive input vectors with a truncated computation in a permuted Haar-wavelet domain, retaining only a subset of transformed coefficient-input pairs. It costs the per-vector permutation and Haar transform computation, storage or transmission of permutation metadata, and a controllable but nonzero approximation error. It can fail if the retained-pair budget needed for acceptable accuracy negates the memory-traffic savings, if energy does not concentrate after sorting on real input distributions, or if metadata overhead dominates at moderate vector dimensions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift
item.description: SchemaShield-Lite replaces naive retry or model retraining as the response to interface drift in tool-augmented agents, wrapping the model's function-calling output with schema validation, candidate-set retry for missing tool names, and one-shot constrained repair. It costs additional inference calls on repair attempts, a modest increase in orchestration complexity, and depends on access to the candidate tool list and schemas at inference time. It can fail when the true failure is semantic rather than interface-level, when candidate-set drift is not the dominant damage mode in the reader's deployment, or when the repair call itself produces an invalid or wrong tool selection, although the paper reports no observed repair harms on its benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape
item.description: The paper does not propose a method to replace anything; it provides non-NTK theory explaining why low-rank LoRA updates suffice, showing that optimal update rank is bounded by a 'bottleneck rank' induced by frozen activations and by attention-specific invariances, not by sample size. It costs nothing to apply directly, since it introduces no new algorithm, but acting on it requires computing or estimating bottleneck ranks of frozen feature maps, which is nontrivial engineering. It can fail as practical guidance because the rank bounds are upper bounds under trace-norm or perturbed objectives, so the theoretically sufficient rank may still exceed what a given task needs, and empirical LoRA rank selection remains heuristic. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Monitor-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries
item.description: The method replaces informal trust that safety monitors' detector outputs reach enforcement points with fixed canary contracts: confirmation units that place a known payload on a changed evidence surface and record both monitor visibility and the downstream decision. It costs only small deterministic test fixtures and negative controls wired into CI against schemas, streams, tools, and adapters, with negligible runtime overhead since the tests run on framework upgrades rather than in the serving path. It can fail to catch failures outside the canaried surfaces, give false assurance if canaries are not updated when frameworks add new evidence paths, and its findings transfer only partially to closed or third-party-hosted frameworks whose internals the reader cannot instrument. 0 independent implementations, 1573 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: GUMPIM: Unitary and Malleable Memory for Processing-in-Memory with Guaranteed PIM Pages
item.description: GUMPIM replaces PIM memory management that either isolates PIM regions or disables memory interleaving, instead letting interleaved CPU pages and contiguous non-interleaved PIM pages coexist in one address space with zero-copy offloading. The cost is new DRAM-side interface hardware for dynamic address mapping plus OS-level dual-track page allocation, translation, and PIM-assisted page migration, with claims validated only on simulated or prototype PIM platforms. It can fail in practice because PIM-enabled HBM/LPDDR hardware is not commercially available at scale, the gains are confined to PIM-suitable workloads, and the technique does not touch GPU or API-based inference at all. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
item.description: ConQUESTA replaces one-shot saliency ranking of QNN entanglers with a constrained mask search in which each candidate pruning mask is fully transpiled across hardware coupling topologies, combining task saliency with compiler cost. The cost is post-training search overhead per mask (transpilation and re-evaluation under an accuracy constraint), plus a fixed-mask recovery step needed to reach feasibility in 22 of 24 runs. It can fail when pruning masks are infeasible for a given topology or when accuracy drops exceed the constraint on small datasets, and it applies only to quantum circuits of 4-12 qubits on simulators or NISQ hardware. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: GatewayBench: Unified Capability and Security Evaluation Platform for MCP Gateways
item.description: GatewayBench replaces ad hoc or absent evaluation of MCP gateway middleware with a standardized benchmark of 524 tasks and 11,118 real tools, comparing flattened and hierarchical gateway architectures under controlled tool-surface scaling. Adopting it costs engineering time to integrate the benchmark harness with the team's gateway and agent stack, plus API or inference spend to run the task suite; it provides evaluation only and improves no production metric by itself. Results can fail to transfer because gateway rankings interact strongly with the underlying model and agent harness, so conclusions drawn with one model may not hold for the reader's production configuration. 2 independent implementations, 1695 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
item.description: It replaces both hosted literature assistants that require sending unpublished work to third parties and naive fixed top-k retrieve-then-answer pipelines, which the paper reports score below the unaided model. Costs include serving an open-weight model locally, building and maintaining the corpus and citation-graph index, and operating the agent harness with its tool and reading components, which adds engineering complexity beyond plain RAG. It can fail on corpora or question types different from the evaluation set, the abstention behavior means a substantial fraction of out-of-corpus questions go unanswered, and gains depend on the harness rather than the model, so a poorly configured deployment may not reproduce the reported accuracy. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: HBFSim: A Simulator for Exploring HBF in Memory Hierarchies for LLMs
item.description: HBFSim is an event-driven simulator that replaces guesswork or ad-hoc profiling when evaluating hypothetical HBM+HBF memory hierarchies for LLM decoding; it does not replace any production component, since HBF hardware is not yet commercially available. It costs engineering time to configure and calibrate against a serving frontend, and its results are only as reliable as the assumed, unpublished HBF device parameters. Conclusions drawn today can fail because real HBF latency, bandwidth, and endurance characteristics may diverge from the modeled values, and the finding that HBM should hold running KV cache rather than cache HBF may not transfer to other workloads or devices. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MLOps-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Production ML Engineering in Real Repositories
item.description: MLOps-Bench replaces generic issue-fixing or competition-style ML agent evaluations with 212 executable lifecycle tasks (data pipelines, training, serving, monitoring, CI/CD, governance) drawn from 31 real repositories, each with oracle patches, buggy baselines, and fail-to-pass/pass-to-pass tests. Adoption costs only the infrastructure to run repository environments and agent rollouts, fitting a single-GPU or API-based setup, but requires engineering effort to integrate the harness into internal agent selection. It can fail as a decision tool if its public repositories diverge from the reader's private stack, and pass rates may not transfer to proprietary codebases or frameworks outside the benchmark's coverage. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
item.description: SkillBrowser replaces static retrieval of skills from the initial task query, and one-shot LLM-based catalog selection, with a Meta-Skill that identifies emerging capability needs during reasoning, issues targeted queries, and loads skills on demand. It costs an additional orchestration layer plus extra LLM calls, which the paper acknowledges as added latency and added inference expense per task. It can fail through under-invocation of useful skills, and its benefits are model- and task-dependent, so weaker base models may not formulate effective skill queries. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: An Interactive GraphRAG Workspace for Reifying, Auditing, and Steering Conversational AI Memories
item.description: It replaces raw concatenation of linear chat histories and flat-vector retrieval with a distilled Goal/Fact/Code fact-graph, a temporal drift auditor, and a gesture-to-prompt compiler. The costs are substantial: an interactive UI layer, 60+ drift heuristics plus calendar-anchored LLM verification calls per audit, and an extraction pipeline that adds latency and ongoing maintenance beyond a simple vector store. Failure modes include incorrect fact distillation silently losing or corrupting technical decisions, regex-based drift detection producing false positives or missed API changes, and the claim being validated on a research prototype rather than the reader's production workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility
item.description: BMuon replaces the Muon optimizer's spectral-norm geometry with a shared channel-allocation budget so that models trained with it retain accuracy under structured MLP pruning, with allocations also serving as a pruning criterion. It costs a modified optimizer with a minorization-maximization surrogate step, applies only when the reader trains models from scratch, and adds implementation complexity over standard Muon or AdamW. It can fail if the budget is set too tight, degrading baseline training quality, and its benefits are irrelevant to readers who only fine-tune or consume pretrained models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Darwin-Claw: Environment-Adaptive Experience Consolidation for Recursively Self-Evolving Agents
item.description: Darwin-Claw replaces indiscriminate injection of raw interaction trajectories into agent memory and skill modules with a hierarchical consolidation pipeline that distills episodic experience into error attributions and prototype vectors used as context patches and skill-update signals. The cost is an additional offline evolver-critic processing stage per interaction cycle, meaning extra LLM calls (API spend or GPU time), new storage for prototype vectors, and added system complexity in the memory layer. It can fail through incorrect error attribution propagating into flawed prototype updates, benchmark overfitting since gains are shown only on the authors' own WildClawBench, and uncontrolled memory drift over long-horizon continual updates. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
item.description: TIDER replaces purely lexical/semantic retrieval over agent long-term memory (and approaches that inject time only at organization or generation) with an RL-trained temporal interval locator whose predicted windows define a temporal retrieval channel, merged with semantic results and reranked by temporal proximity. The cost is training a 1.7B locator with composite RL rewards (feasible on a 24 GB GPU but non-trivial engineering), plus added retrieval latency and pipeline complexity from the dual-channel merge and reranking. It can fail when queries lack identifiable temporal structure, when timestamps in memory are noisy or missing, or when the locator mispredicts windows and excludes the correct evidence before the semantic channel can compensate; benchmark gains on LifeBench/LoCoMo may not transfer to other memory distributions. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
item.description: CDSE replaces monolithic skill artifacts in self-improving agents with a unified skill split into four coordinated components (Meta, Experience, Tool, Script), updated separately from semantic gradients extracted from successful and failed trajectories. The cost is a more complex skill-maintenance pipeline: component-specific extraction, consolidation, validation, cross-component coordination, and adaptive invocation logic, plus additional LLM calls for trajectory analysis and update generation. It can fail if trajectory evidence is sparse or unrepresentative, if component updates conflict despite coordination, or if the benchmark gains do not transfer to the reader's narrower production task distribution. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding
item.description: Replaces dense speculative decoding's per-token target verification with a sparse scheme where the draft generates most tokens and a lightweight logistic predictor over aggregate trajectory-shape confidence features decides when to invoke the target for short corrective segments. Costs: training the trigger predictor on draft correctness labels, maintaining a draft-target pair, and added orchestration complexity; target compute drops substantially, but absolute latency savings versus dense baselines are not quantified in the abstract. Fails when local early evidence is too weak to predict trajectory failure (the stated timing tradeoff) or when the target model lacks competence on the task, in which case the method loses to open-loop baselines, as observed on MATH-500. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
item.description: The framework replaces the unaudited use of LLM-generated stakeholder weights as inputs to multi-objective optimization with an explicit reliability assessment plus robust weighted-sum optimization under preference uncertainty. It costs additional inference calls for eliciting explicit and implicit preferences across roles and conditions, statistical modeling of pairwise choices, and solving robust rather than nominal optimization models, with no claim of reduced compute or latency. It can fail because deliberation among agents erases legitimate role differences, pairwise choices are dominated by presentation order rather than context, and contextual predictive models add little over order alone, so the elicited preferences may not reflect real stakeholder trade-offs even after auditing. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
item.description: GLOBE replaces monolithic prompt optimization for generative-search listing rewriting with an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped behaviors maintained by Editor, Reflector, Moderator, and Curator roles. The cost is multiple additional LLM calls per episode (reflection, moderation, curation) plus the complexity of maintaining and validating a persistent behavior store, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU via APIs but increasing token spend. It can fail if rank-based feedback is noisy or sparse, causing harmful behaviors to be committed before deactivation catches them, and the demonstrated benefit is specific to e-commerce listing optimization rather than a general agent-memory result. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
item.description: DLite replaces conventional draft models that maintain their own historical KV cache with a history-free draft that reuses the target model's contextual hidden states and a lightweight sequential head, trained with a two-stage strategy. It costs the training of a custom draft head, access to the target model's hidden states, and integration effort into the serving stack, though it reduces draft-side KV memory overhead. It can fail on workloads where acceptance length does not reach the reported 2-6 range, and it is inapplicable to API-only models that do not expose hidden states. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
item.description: DrugHarness replaces static, hand-configured scientific agent pipelines with a tool-composing harness that induces, reviews, and revises reusable skills from execution trajectories. It costs a curated environment of over 80 scientific operations and biomedical resources, an additional review agent for skill verification and targeted execution trials, plus ongoing skill-library maintenance; it does not require foundation-model training, so a single-GPU or API-based deployment is feasible for the LLM component, but the scientific tooling itself carries licensing and compute demands. It can fail through induction of spurious skills from noisy execution feedback, overfitting to benchmark-like tasks, and wet-lab validation results that do not generalize beyond the reported HPK1 case. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
item.description: It replaces standard last-token hidden-state embeddings from frozen LLMs with representations from which layer-wise low-rank language-specific subspaces (estimated from parallel-sentence residuals) have been removed. The cost is inference-time overhead: a one-time subspace estimation requiring multilingual parallel sentences plus a per-layer projection at embedding time, with no fine-tuning. It can fail if parallel data for the target language pair is unavailable or unrepresentative, if the low-rank assumption removes semantically relevant components, or if gains do not transfer to languages or models outside the evaluated set. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding
item.description: The recommendation is to keep lossless verification in speculative decoding rather than adopting training-free relaxed (lossy) acceptance rules, and to evaluate decoding efficiency by wall-clock time, verifier rounds, and completion length instead of accepted tokens per round. Lossless verification preserves the target distribution at the cost of lower per-round acceptance, while relaxed rules inflate reasoning traces and can exhaust the token budget before a final answer is produced. Relaxed rules can fail by accepting low-probability draft tokens that extend completions, reduce verifier rounds at the price of substantial accuracy loss, and deliver no real latency improvement despite favorable headline acceptance metrics. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
item.description: The method replaces costly manual reproduction and robustness checking of published statistical findings with LLM agents that execute analyses and systematically vary analytical choices. It costs API-level LLM spend plus engineering effort to build a domain-grounded benchmark (here, 20 SEER-based papers) and to curate executable baselines, with no large-scale training required. It can fail on the roughly 22% of claims not reproduced, on agents proposing indefensible alternative analyses, and by generating false-positive flags that consume expert review time. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Delay Complexity Dimension: Learning with Delayed and Censored Labels
item.description: This is a PAC learning-theoretic characterization of training with delayed and censored labels rather than a deployable method, so it replaces nothing in an existing inference or training stack; the adjacent practical artifacts are a quantization scheme and an expedition (label-expediting) policy that could supplement standard delayed-feedback pipelines such as conversion modeling. The cost of acting on it is engineering effort to integrate pseudo-labeling, quantization of delay information, or expedition policies into the data pipeline, plus dependence on assumptions (oracle pseudo-labels, instance-family-specific rates) that may not hold on real traffic. What can fail after adoption is that the achievable-rate question remains open where DCD and classical censored-ERM complexity separate, the labeler-diversity prediction failed empirically in a budget-matched test, and the window-beats-immediate-labels phenomenon is regime-dependent rather than universal. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Discovering Undisclosed Concepts in LoRA Adapters for Diffusion-Based AIGC Models
item.description: The method replaces exhaustive prompt-space exploration and brute-force render-and-inspect auditing of LoRA adapters with a render-free subspace-alignment filter (SGES) that shortlists candidate prompts, followed by paired LoRA-versus-base rendering (PVI) only on that shortlist. Its cost is a single diffusion model plus adapter on one GPU, an evolutionary search loop, and a small number of verification renders, so it is feasible on a 24 GB GPU but adds engineering complexity in the alignment scoring and search implementation. It can fail when the adapter's concept is not well exposed by any single conditioning prompt, when the subspace-alignment proxy misranks genuinely revealing prompts, or when the base model already produces similar outputs, weakening the distinctiveness signal. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Discrete Diffusion Models are Minimax Optimal Under Sparsity
item.description: This is a statistical theory result: it analyzes a nonparametric estimator from a regularized score-entropy objective and proves minimax-optimal convergence rates under sparsity, so it replaces nothing in a production stack. Adoption cost is not applicable because there is no deployable method, trained model, or engineering artifact; the label-smoothing-like regularization is a theoretical device, not a validated training recipe. The only practical risk is misreading the result as evidence that production discrete diffusion models automatically adapt to sparsity, which the minimax analysis of an idealized estimator does not establish. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
item.description: JSSA replaces full-KV attention during long-context decoding with training-free token-level sparse selection scored in a learned shared low-dimensional query-key subspace, executed via a gather-free indexed-attention kernel compatible with the standard GQA KV-cache layout. The cost is integrating a custom kernel and computing the subspace projection per model, plus residual selection overhead; the subspace is derived from a closed-form spectral solution, so there is no training pipeline to maintain. It can fail if the low-dimensional scoring loses ranking structure on out-of-distribution workloads, if the kernel is unavailable or unoptimized for the reader's hardware (gains were demonstrated on a B200, not a 24 GB consumer GPU), or if competing sparse methods' generation-length inflation reappears on atypical prompts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: How Many Ranks Does a Token Need? A Noise-Floor Squelch for Rank-One LoRA Experts
item.description: Replaces the fixed-rank LoRA update and learned top-k routers of mixture-of-LoRA methods with a router-free soft-thresholding of each token's rank-one responses, with the threshold chosen per module by Stein's unbiased risk estimate and a Gram-matrix explaining-away step, adding no trainable parameters. Cost is an extra per-token response computation, robust noise estimation, and a value Gram solve at inference, plus implementation complexity beyond a standard LoRA stack; training cost is comparable to LoRA since thresholds are set post hoc per module. It can fail if the Gaussian noise-floor assumption does not hold for a given adapter or domain, if coherence among co-active components is high enough to degrade the explaining-away step, or if the reported gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated models and benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
item.description: LayerTrim replaces training-based structured pruning pipelines (e.g., RESP) with a training-free method that trims MLP features in redundant decoder layers while preserving attention blocks and depth, yielding a smaller dense model. It costs implementation effort for the layer-selection and trimming procedure and incurs some accuracy loss relative to the dense model, though less than competing pruning methods; no recovery training or extra GPU memory is required. It can fail on reasoning workloads or model families not covered in the evaluation, since long-form reasoning accuracy (e.g., AIME) is sensitive to layer removal and the reported gains come from a single study on three models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Adaptive Computation with Conformal Certification
