item.description: The method replaces uniform full-resolution dense inference (and uniform efficiency techniques such as quantization and pruning) with hierarchical prediction: a low-resolution model proposes regions, conformal risk control certifies which regions contain signal, and computation is spent refining only certified regions. The cost is a two-stage hierarchical architecture plus a conformal calibration procedure requiring labeled calibration data and a chosen risk target, adding pipeline and validation complexity beyond a single dense model. Failure modes include miscertification if the calibration distribution shifts from deployment data, missed sparse signals that the low-resolution stage fails to propose, and speedups that may not materialize on data where relevant content is not spatially sparse. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
item.description: The method replaces full attention over distant tokens with recurrent fixed-size neural memory modules updated at test time, while retaining full-fidelity attention over a recent block via a blockwise attention mask. It requires a post-training retrofit phase rather than pretraining from scratch, adds test-time parameter updates that increase implementation and serving complexity, and was validated only on a 1B model with medium context lengths. Failure modes include loss of precise recall of distant details compressed into the memory modules, sensitivity to block size and memory capacity, and uncertain transfer of the gains to larger models or very long contexts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
item.description: ProD replaces plain supervised fine-tuning on teacher trajectories with an iterative distillation procedure that detects stagnation in student trajectories and adds an adaptive margin penalty to discourage unproductive loops. Costs include access to a teacher model for trajectory comparison, stagnation detection and margin computation during training, and iterative training rounds; on a single 24 GB GPU this is feasible for 0.6B-8B students with parameter-efficient fine-tuning but adds training complexity and time. It can fail if teacher trajectories are unavailable for the target domain, if the stagnation detector misfires and penalizes legitimate exploration, or if the student is too small to absorb the corrected behavior. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains
item.description: Replaces trusting a downloaded GGUF solely via its full-precision weight signature with a protocol that re-derives the quantized artifact bit-for-bit from disclosed inputs, requiring the builder to record and ship the floating-point-contraction setting, per-tensor quantization recipes, and a hash-bound calibration imatrix. It costs negligible model quality (+0.06% perplexity from the unique-output compiler setting), adds build-provenance bookkeeping, and requires the verifier to rerun quantization locally on a 24 GB GPU, which is feasible for GGUF-class models. It fails when providers omit build-environment coordinates (currently universal: IVR 0/198), against targeted embedding edits that evade divergence statistics, and against adversarial-fp16 attacks, which lie outside the protocol. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference
item.description: PN-Mix replaces fixed-precision or purely key-statistics-based mixed-precision KV cache quantization with saliency allocation driven by query-key pair-norm products at the RoPE channel-pair level, identified once during prefill and reused during decoding. The cost is a one-time prefill saliency analysis, implementation of per-channel-pair mixed-precision kernels, and residual accuracy loss at very low bit rates compared to full-precision caching. It can fail on non-RoPE or non-decoder-only architectures, on workloads whose saliency profile shifts between prefill and long decoding, and if custom kernel overhead negates the memory-bandwidth savings on a single-GPU serving stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DAGFormer: Global Topology Prediction for Transformer Cross-Layer Connections
item.description: DAGFormer replaces the fixed residual-connection topology of a standard Transformer with token-conditioned cross-layer connections whose strengths are planned globally by a jointly trained topology predictor, so it must be incorporated at pretraining time rather than retrofitted to existing checkpoints. The cost is an additional predictor module, extra connection parameters, modified training code, and a full pretraining run from scratch, with all reported evidence limited to models at or below 1B parameters trained on up to 10B tokens. What can fail is unverified scaling behavior beyond 1B, incompatibility with off-the-shelf pretrained checkpoints and optimized inference stacks, and the possibility that input-dependent routing gains do not transfer to domains or data mixtures unlike the paper's setup. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ESL-former: Event Sparse Linear Transformer for FPGA-Accelerated Malware Detection
item.description: The method replaces explicit quadratic attention and binary-mask sparse execution with a linear transformer whose accumulated key-value state is used to score and prune tokens and channels, reorganized by a Top-K buffer and hardware compaction unit into dense streams for FPGA multiply-accumulate arrays. The cost is a custom FPGA accelerator design, a contribution-aware scoring and compaction pipeline, and dependence on linear attention rather than standard softmax attention. It can fail if the contribution-based pruning discards tokens needed for rare malware variants, and its gains do not transfer to GPU or API-based deployments. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
item.description: CAFE replaces two's-complement weight/activation encoding in FeFET-based compute-in-memory arrays with a selectively allocated differential encoding guided by a conducting-cell activity metric and NSGA-II search. The cost is 1.86-2.78x normalized array/encoding overhead plus a per-layer optimization and pruning pipeline, and accuracy still falls short of the ideal full-differential configuration in some layers. The method can fail if device variation statistics shift across chips or process conditions, invalidating the C2AM-guided allocation, and it presumes access to FeFET CIM hardware that the reader does not have. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ReGRA: Residual-Gradient Adaptation for Complementary Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
item.description: ReGRA replaces a single-stage LoRA update with two complementary low-rank stages: a standard first-stage adapter, then a second adapter initialized from residual task gradients projected away from the first-stage subspace, with an orthogonality regularizer. It costs an extra fine-tuning stage, a calibration set, and gradient-estimation compute, but merges into the base weights with no inference overhead. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative, if the residual-gradient estimate is noisy on small datasets, or if the two-stage pipeline's added hyperparameters are not retuned for the target task. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Discriminative Score Function: Turning Pretrained Models into Functional Generative Priors
item.description: DSF replaces diffusion-style generative models or real calibration data by deriving a training-free image-space score field from the loss gradients of an existing pretrained discriminative model, usable for synthesis, editing, inpainting, and zero-shot quantization calibration. It costs only gradient computations through an already-deployed model, but sampling is an iterative gradient-ascent procedure with per-sample latency, and image fidelity is unlikely to match dedicated generative models. It can fail when the discriminative model's implicit manifold trace is weak or task-narrow, producing calibration samples whose distribution mismatch degrades quantized-model accuracy on real data. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Poisoning Attacks on Flow-Based Intrusion Detection
item.description: The method replaces blind trust in IDS training pipelines with a diagnostic-first workflow: constrained perturbation analysis localizes trigger-relevant features, behavioral drift is measured against a distilled baseline, and mitigation proceeds via automated data sanitization or neuron pruning rather than full retraining. Costs include maintaining a distilled reference model, running perturbation analyses per model, and engineering effort to integrate sanitization or pruning into the data pipeline; the pruning step can also degrade clean-input accuracy if applied aggressively. It can fail against triggers that evade the chosen perturbation constraints, against poisoning that does not produce measurable drift relative to the baseline, and it is inapplicable when the reader consumes third-party API models whose weights and training data are inaccessible. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Computational compressive imaging reconstruction with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver
item.description: The method replaces gradient-based compressed sensing algorithms and neural network reconstruction for single-pixel and lensless imaging with an Ising-model formulation whose Hamiltonian is minimized by a simulated-annealing solver. It costs the engineering effort of encoding the inverse problem as an Ising Hamiltonian plus auxiliary sparsity and smoothness constraints, with reconstruction quality reported as comparable to or better than mainstream algorithms but no quantified speedup or energy figure in the abstract. It can fail because simulated annealing offers no convergence guarantees to the ground state, scales poorly on general-purpose hardware, and the claimed compute and power benefits depend on dedicated Ising-machine hardware that is not commercially accessible. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
item.description: Replaces standard draft-verify speculative decoding (e.g., EAGLE-style or DSpark) with a draft model trained for intra-block self-correction, next-block foresight drafting, and pipelined overlap of drafting and verification, while preserving the target model's output distribution. Costs include training the self-refining draft model, integrating a custom pipelined serving path, and additional memory for the draft model alongside the target. It can fail if acceptance rates drop on out-of-domain workloads, negating speedup; if released draft models do not cover the reader's target model, requiring training the reader cannot afford; and because headline numbers were measured on a GB200, gains on a single 24 GB GPU are unvalidated. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Delta Tokenizer: Reference-Identical Tokenization of Session Deltas and Segment-Parallelism for Long Prompts on Multicore CPUs
item.description: Replaces full re-tokenization of each request with reuse of the prior session's token sequence, re-encoding only the appended text and a boundary tail, with an exact parallel chunking path for cold long prompts. Cost is additional CPU-side state per session (retained token sequences), integration into the serving front end (currently demonstrated in SGLang), and a shared CPU pool scheduler that adds operational complexity. It can fail if sessions are short-lived or prompts change mid-conversation rather than by pure append, if CPU cores are already saturated by the tokenizer pool, or if tokenizer versions diverge between stored state and the serving engine. 0 independent implementations, 6 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: adopt.
